items.title: US weighs new Iran strikes after the midterms while Qatar pushes a draft deal
items.summary: Al Jazeera (30 October) reports the US and Israel have drawn up plans to strike Iran after the 3 November midterms, citing the New York Times, while Vice President Vance has reached out proposing direct talks. CBS says Qatari mediators presented Iran with a new draft deal to end the war. Iranian state TV claims three tankers exploded while crossing the Strait of Hormuz; that claim is unverified, so treat the picture as provisional.
items.why: Gulf escalation or a deal moves oil prices, which feed into corporate budgets, hiring and marketing spend.

items.title: Ceasefire in a southern Ukrainian city held its first day, with US-led talks planned (3 days old)
items.summary: The Washington Times (28 October, three days old) reported a six-day ceasefire in and around a Russia-occupied southern city held through its first day and night, though fighting continued elsewhere. US-led plans to bring Moscow and Kyiv back for technical talks next month were reported with no firm date. No newer Ukraine update was found, so this is early and provisional.
items.why: Progress on Ukraine affects energy prices and sanctions, which global employers plan around.

items.title: Inflation sits at its highest in about two years after the RBI's rate hike (October context)
items.summary: No India story dated 31 October turned up, so this is October context. Trading Economics reports the RBI raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% in October, its first hike since February 2023, and puts September CPI inflation at 5.54%, the highest since October 2024. The RBI's own release cites a lower August figure of 4.8%, so the latest number is provisional; check the RBI's release.
items.why: Higher rates and prices raise company costs and can slow campus hiring and consumer spending.

items.title: RBI projects CPI inflation near 5.8% and raised its FY27 growth forecast to 7.1%
items.summary: Trading Economics reports the RBI expects headline CPI to average almost 5.8% over the next three quarters and raised its FY2026/27 GDP growth forecast to 7.1% from 6.7%. A single aggregator source, so provisional.
items.why: Strong growth with sticky inflation shapes salary and hiring expectations.

items.title: Sensex and Nifty extend their recovery on Friday as IT and pharma gain
items.summary: BusinessToday (30 October) reports the Sensex and Nifty extended their recovery, with the Sensex up about 0.6% near 74,629 and the Nifty about 0.7% near 23,098 in intraday trade, helped by IT, pharma and results from Trent and IndiGo. Analysts flagged elevated crude, West Asia tensions and continued FII selling as limits. Markets are shut on Saturday, and these are intraday levels rather than closing figures, so treat them as provisional.
items.why: Market sentiment changes recruiters' risk appetite and campus-hiring plans.

items.title: Reliance Industries' Q2 results are the next big market trigger
items.summary: One market report names Reliance's Q2 results, oil prices and global cues as what will guide sentiment next. A single secondary source, so provisional.
items.why: A heavyweight's earnings often set the tone for the whole index.

items.title: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and Anthropic back one shared AI-training opt-out signal
items.summary: AI Weekly reports that on 30 October the four companies said they will honour a single robots.txt token that lets a site opt out of AI training across all their crawlers. Rollout differs: Anthropic says it has begun, Microsoft targets 1 February 2027, Google says 2027 and OpenAI says coming months. This comes from an aggregator, so provisional.
items.why: Content rights and data consent are becoming marketing and brand-policy issues.

items.title: OpenAI reportedly plans to buy Google's AI chips
items.summary: A Venture Daily Digest roundup reports OpenAI plans to purchase Google's Tensor Processing Units, expanding a relationship that already includes renting them. The same roundup says Amazon could make over $100 billion from Anthropic's IPO. Newsletter-sourced and unconfirmed, so provisional.
items.why: Shifting compute alliances change which AI vendors employers hire for and partner with.

items.title: Nvidia will guarantee Nscale's debt for a 460 MW Anthropic build
items.summary: AI Weekly lists Nvidia guaranteeing Nscale debt for Anthropic's 460 MW build among 30 October's top AI stories. A headline-level item from one aggregator, so provisional.
items.why: Shows how capital-heavy AI infrastructure has become.
